en: Full are the heavens and the earth
of the majesty of your glory.
You throughout the circle of the lands
You, king of glory, O Christ.
You are the everlasting Son of the Father.
You, when you were to take up man to set him free,
did not shrink from the Virgin's womb.
You, the sting of death overcome,
opened to believers the kingdoms of the heavens.
You sit at the right hand of God,
in the glory of the Father.
You are believed to be the judge who will come.
come to the help of your servants,
whom you have redeemed with precious blood.
Make them, with your saints, in eternal
And rule them, and lift them up
Through each single day we bless you;
into the age, and into the age of the age.
on this day to keep us without sin.
Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us.
as we have hoped in you.
In you, Lord, I have hoped:
let me not be put to shame for ever.
notes: General: the accents in the Latin (laudámus, Dóminum) only mark stress for singing; they do not change the sense.

lines 1-4 and 14-21: the Latin puts 'Te' (you) first and the verb last; that order is kept, so 'You … the choir of the apostles, the number of the prophets, the army of martyrs praises' is one sentence over lines 14-19.
line 2: 'confitemur' means to acknowledge, confess or profess (as one's Lord).
line 7: 'potestates', the powers, are an order of angels.
line 11: 'Sabaoth' is a Hebrew word kept in the Latin: hosts, armies (of heaven).
line 18: 'candidatus', clothed in white (the white robes of the martyrs).
line 20: 'per orbem terrarum', literally 'through the circle of the lands', i.e. throughout the whole world.
line 26: 'Paraclete', from the Greek: advocate, helper, comforter.
line 29: 'susceptúrus hóminem', about to take on (human nature as) man; 'ad liberandum', in order to set free.

lines 39-40: one clause: 'make them be numbered with your saints in eternal glory'. 'Aeterna' agrees with 'gloria' on the next line. Older manuscripts read 'munerari' (be rewarded) where this text has 'numerari' (be numbered).
line 47: 'in saeculum, et in saeculum saeculi', literally 'into the age, and into the age of the age': for ever and ever.
line 55: 'confundar', be confounded, put to shame, brought to ruin.
